parts.label: (a)(i)
key_concepts: amplitude as maximum displacement from equilibrium
reading peak and equilibrium values from displacement-time graph
hints: Hint 1: Look at Fig. 4.2 for the first few oscillations - where is the middle line the oscillation is centred on, and how far do the peaks go above and below it?
parts.proper_answer: Equilibrium $L_0 = 20\text{ cm}$, extremes $25\text{ cm}$ and $15\text{ cm}$, so amplitude $x_0 = 25 - 20 = 5.0\text{ cm}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Find the equilibrium line**
Think of amplitude as the maximum distance from the centre of the motion, not the total top-to-bottom swing. In Fig. 4.2 the early undamped oscillations go between $L = 25\text{ cm}$ and $L = 15\text{ cm}$. The centre is halfway between: $$L_0 = \frac{25+15}{2} = 20\text{ cm}$$

Step 2: **Subtract to get amplitude**
Amplitude is peak minus equilibrium: $$x_0 = 25 - 20 = 5.0\text{ cm}$$ A common slip is to give $10\text{ cm}$ which is the peak-to-peak range, twice the amplitude.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
hints: Hint 1: Focus on the undamped part at the start of Fig. 4.2 - how long does one full repeat from one peak to the next peak take?
Hint 2: Recall how angular frequency $\omega$ is linked to period $T$ for SHM, then substitute your value of $T$ with correct units.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Measure the period T**
One oscillation is peak to next peak or trough to next trough. From Fig. 4.2 peaks are at $t = 0, 4.0, 8.0\text{ s}$, so: $$T = 4.0\text{ s}$$ Use the early part where damping has not started, so the period is clear.

Step 2: **Convert period to angular frequency**
For SHM the angle swept per second is: $$\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T}$$ $$\omega = \frac{2\pi}{4.0} \approx 1.6\text{ rad s}^{-1}$$ Keep $\omega$ in $\text{rad s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
key_concepts: maximum speed in SHM v0 = omega x0
consistent units for amplitude and speed
hints: Hint 1: Think about where speed is largest in SHM - at the centre - and which two quantities you have already found that control it.
Hint 2: Check the relation $v_0 = \omega x_0$ and make sure $x_0$ is in cm if you want $v_0$ in $\text{cm s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Recall the SHM speed rule**
Maximum speed happens as you rush through equilibrium, and for SHM it is simply: $$v_0 = \omega x_0$$ where $x_0$ is amplitude.

Step 2: **Substitute your values**
Use $x_0 = 5.0\text{ cm}$ and $\omega = 1.57\text{ rad s}^{-1}$: $$v_0 = 1.57 \times 5.0 \approx 7.9\text{ cm s}^{-1}$$ If you use $\omega = 1.6$, you get $8.0\text{ cm s}^{-1}$ which is also accepted within rounding. Keeping cm gives $\text{cm s}^{-1}$ directly.

parts.label: (b)
hints: Hint 1: Start at $t = 0$ in Fig. 4.2 - is $L$ at its maximum, minimum or middle, and what does that tell you about which way the trolley was first pulled?
Hint 2: Compare the shape from $t = 0$ to $12\text{ s}$ with the shape after $12\text{ s}$ - what stays the same and what starts to shrink?
Hint 3: Think about what switching off the air blower does to friction, and why the peaks still come at regular time intervals even as they get smaller.
parts.proper_answer: Any three from: trolley initially pulled to right (towards Y) and released from rest at $L=25\text{ cm}$; equilibrium at $L=20\text{ cm}$; period $4.0\text{ s}$ constant; motion undamped $0$ to $12\text{ s}$ then lightly damped after $12\text{ s}$ when blower switched off; amplitude decreases after $12\text{ s}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Read the start of the story**
At $t=0$, $L = 25\text{ cm}$ which is the maximum distance from X. So you pulled the trolley to the right, toward Y, and let go. The motion is centred on $L = 20\text{ cm}$, the equilibrium position.

Step 2: **Spot undamped then damped**
From $t = 0$ to about $t = 12\text{ s}$ the peaks stay at $25\text{ cm}$ and troughs at $15\text{ cm}$. That constant amplitude means no energy loss - undamped SHM on the air cushion. After $12\text{ s}$ the peaks shrink toward $20\text{ cm}$. That is damping starting when the air blower is switched off and friction returns.

Step 3: **Describe the damping**
The amplitude falls gradually but the time between peaks stays about $4.0\text{ s}$. That is the signature of light damping - energy is lost slowly and period is almost unaffected. You can also note maximum speed at $1\text{ s}, 3\text{ s}$ etc. when passing through $20\text{ cm}$, and momentarily stationary at $2\text{ s}, 4\text{ s}$ etc. at the extremes.

parts.label: (c)
key_concepts: closed elliptical loop for undamped oscillation
maximum speed at equilibrium, zero speed at extremes
hints: Hint 1: For the first oscillation there is no damping, so the $v$ against $L$ trace must close back on itself - what $L$ value should it be centred on?
Hint 2: Mark the left and right ends of the loop from part (a)(i) - where is $v = 0$ and what are the $L$ limits?
Hint 3: Mark the top and bottom of the loop from part (a)(iii) - where is speed largest, and is $v$ positive or negative as $L$ first falls from $25\text{ cm}$?
parts.proper_answer: Closed (elliptical) loop centred on $(20\text{ cm}, 0)$, extending horizontally from $L = 15\text{ cm}$ to $L = 25\text{ cm}$ with $v = 0$ at both ends, and vertically from $v = -7.9\text{ cm s}^{-1}$ to $v = +7.9\text{ cm s}^{-1}$ with $|v|$ maximum at $L = 20\text{ cm}$. Starts at $(25,0)$ moving to negative $v$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Picture the shape**
Plotting velocity against displacement for undamped SHM always gives a closed loop. Here the horizontal axis is $L$, not $x$, so the loop is centred on the equilibrium $(L_0,0) = (20\text{ cm}, 0)$, not on zero.

Step 2: **Fix the horizontal ends**
At the turning points the trolley momentarily stops. So at $L = 15\text{ cm}$ and $L = 25\text{ cm}$, $v = 0$. Draw the loop touching the $L$-axis exactly at those two points.

Step 3: **Fix the vertical top and bottom**
Speed is maximum when rushing through the middle $L = 20\text{ cm}$. From (a)(iii) that is about $7.9\text{ cm s}^{-1}$. So the loop reaches $v = +7.9\text{ cm s}^{-1}$ and $v = -7.9\text{ cm s}^{-1}$ at $L = 20\text{ cm}$. Since motion starts at $L = 25\text{ cm}$ and $L$ then decreases, initial velocity is in the negative $L$ direction, so the trace leaves $(25,0)$ going downward to negative $v$, round through $(15,0)$, back via positive $v$ to $(25,0)$ in a clockwise sense.
